 - [Citation](#citation \"Citation\")\n\n# [](#spark-x26-4b-eagle-3-draft-head) Spark-X2.6-4B EAGLE-3 draft head\n\nA one-layer EAGLE-3 draft head (218M parameters) for [XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B](https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B). It proposes tokens that the 4B model verifies, so speculative decoding runs faster while the output stays exactly what the target model would have produced.\n\nThere was no public draft head for Spark, so this is a from-scratch one. It is provided so you can combine it with whatever target GGUF you already use.\n\nThis is **v8**, the current release: trained on a mixed code \\+ prose \\+ conversation corpus with verifier-argmax distillation and the EAGLE-3 training-time test.\n\n## [](#⚠️-requires-a-one-line-llamacpp-patch) ⚠️ Requires a one-line llama.cpp patch\n\nllama.cpp's EAGLE-3 draft consumes the *input* to three target decoder layers, exposed per architecture as `res->t_layer_inp[il]`. Spark's arch (`spark2_5`) does not set it, and the runtime aborts with:\n\n```\nGGML_ASSERT(t_layer_inp[il] != nullptr)\n```\n\nApply `llama.cpp-spark2_5-layer-inputs.patch` (included here) to `src/models/spark2-5.cpp` and rebuild:\n\n```diff\n     for (int il = 0; il < n_layer; ++il) {\n+        res->t_layer_inp[il] = inpL;\n+\n         ggml_tensor * inpSA = inpL;\n```\n\nTested against llama.cpp `0.7.0-dev` (commit `f5027fb`).\n\n## [](#quick-start) Quick start\n\n```bash\nllama-server \\\n    --model Spark-X2.6-4B-Q8_0.gguf \\\n    --draft spark-eagle3-v8.gguf --spec-type draft-eagle3 \\\n    --spec-draft-n-max 3 \\\n    -ngl 99 --ngld 99\n```\n\nWhere the 4B target does not fit in VRAM, keep it on the CPU and put only the head on the GPU — the head costs \\~0.5 GiB including a 4k context:\n\n```bash\nllama-server \\\n    --model Spark-X2.6-4B-Q8_0.gguf \\\n    --draft spark-eagle3-v8.gguf --spec-type draft-eagle3 \\\n    --spec-draft-n-max 3 \\\n    --ngl 0 --ngld 99 --threads 4 -c 4096 -np 1\n```\n\n**`--spec-draft-n-max`:** `3` for prose, `2` never, `1` for code. Prose depth-1 acceptance is 0\\.75, so a pass returning \\~3.2 tokens beats verifying four; code depth-1 is \\~0.15, so only n=1 helps there.\n\n**Avoid `2` when the target is on the CPU.** It is not a middle setting: in llama.cpp 0\\.7.0-dev a pass at `n_max 2` costs \\~350 ms against \\~182 ms at `1` and \\~217 ms at `3`, so it lands below both (prose 1\\.28x vs 1\\.84x/2.57x). The same value behaves normally with the target in VRAM, so this is a CPU-side code-path artifact.\n\n## [](#specs) Specs\n\n|  |  |\n| --- | --- |\n| Architecture | EAGLE-3, 1 decoder layer |\n| Parameters | 218M (32k draft vocab dominates) |\n| Base model | `XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B` (Apache-2.0) |\n| Target layers fused | 2, 18, 33 |\n| Hidden size | 2560 |\n| Attention | 16 heads / 4 KV, head\\_dim 256, RoPE theta 1e6 |\n| Draft vocab | 32,000 with `d2t` / `t2d` maps |\n| Weight file | 422 MB bf16 GGUF, 834 MB fp32 safetensors |\n\nNote for anyone loading the safetensors by hand: `d2t` is stored as **deltas** (`convert_hf_to_gguf.py` adds `arange` to recover absolute ids). Exporting absolute ids fails with `EAGLE-3 d2t target ids out of range for target vocab size 131072`.\n\n## [](#training) Training\n\n|  |  |\n| --- | --- |\n| Corpus | 21\\.96M tokens: 10M Python repo code (codeparrot-clean), 3M instruction→code (Magicoder), 2M prose (WikiText-103), 7M conversation (UltraChat-200k, 32% of segments) |\n| Steps | 5,362 (one epoch, batch 4 × 1024) |\n| Objective | CE against the **target's own argmax**, plus 0\\.5 · MSE on the fed-back prenorm state, plus a depth-1 CE from the **training-time test** |\n| Hardware | single RTX 3090 at 300 W, target frozen in bf16 |\n\nThree choices carried the gain, each measured against the previous version:\n\n**Label on the verifier, not the corpus.** Acceptance is `draft argmax == target argmax`, so wherever the corpus token is not what Spark would emit, ordinary cross-entropy teaches a position the draft can never win. Relabelling lifted prose acceptance 0\\.49 → 0\\.81 at identical cost.\n\n**Training-time test.** The head is also fed its own prenorm output back as the next step's `g`, with a second loss there, so it learns to recover from its own drafts. This raised prose depth-1 acceptance 0\\.50 → 0\\.70 and is what makes `n_max > 1` pay.\n\n**Conversational data.** Instruct prose rendered through Spark's own template lifted chat-format acceptance 0\\.299 → 0\\.325 (0.377 with thinking disabled). Templated *code* in the same quantity moved it 0\\.001, so the win is the register, not the markers.\n\n## [](#results) Results\n\nDepth-0 acceptance, greedy, 96-token generations, target in VRAM:\n\n| prompt form | p0 |\n| --- | --- |\n| WikiText prose (in-domain) | 0\\.920 |\n| 12 mixed prompts, raw text | 0\\.464 |\n| 12 mixed prompts, chat template (thinking on) | 0\\.325 |\n| 3 Python code prompts | 0\\.415 |\n\nThroughput, single RTX 3090 \\+ i7-6700K (n=3 unless noted):\n\n| placement | prose | mixed | chat format | code |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Q8 target on CPU (5.79 tok/s), head on GPU | **2\\.57x** | 1\\.48x (n=1) | 1\\.24x (n=1) | – |\n| Q8 target in VRAM (\\~140 tok/s), head on GPU | 2\\.04x | 1\\.18x (n=1) | 1\\.06x (n=1) | 1\\.08x (n=1) |\n\nAt n=1 the CPU placement gives 1\\.88x on prose and 1\\.48x on mixed prompts. The gain scales with how slow the verifier is: with the target in VRAM a token costs \\~7 ms, so the draft's fixed per-pass cost stops being negligible.\n\n## [](#limitations) Limitations\n\n- **Chat format is still weaker than raw text.** 0\\.325 against 0\\.464 on the same prompts: the template opens a thinking channel, and the corpus contains no reasoning traces, so thinking-mode acceptance lags thinking-off (0.377).\n\n- **Narrow out of domain.** 0\\.92 in-domain but 0\\.46 on mixed prompts. A public EAGLE-3 head for Qwen3-4B scored 0\\.53–0.64 on the same mixed/code prompt sets.\n\n- **Code is the weakest domain**, and p1 ≈ 0\\.15 means only `n_max 1` is useful. Code p0 is 0\\.415 here against 0\\.437 for the previous release; that difference is **within the ±0.03 noise of a 3-prompt evaluation** and coincided with cutting the code share from 12M to 10M tokens, so treat it as unresolved rather than real.\n\n- **Two-layer capacity is blocked upstream**: `convert_hf_to_gguf.py` only detects EAGLE-3 at `num_hidden_layers == 1`, and llama.cpp's `eagle3` graph builds one layer, so a deeper head needs patches on both sides.\n\n- **Small evaluation.** 12 hand-written \\+ 12 WikiText \\+ 3 code prompts, in two prompt forms; the mixed and code figures carry roughly ±0.03 uncertainty.\n\n- **Spark only.** The head reads Spark's hidden states at layers 2/18/33 with Spark's tokenizer; it will not work with another model.\n\n## [](#files) Files\n\n| file | purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `spark-eagle3-v8.gguf` | current release, `--spec-type draft-eagle3` |\n| `v8/model.safetensors`, `v8/config.json` | v8 fp32 HF-format checkpoint |\n| `v8/train_log.json` | v8 training curve |\n| `llama.cpp-spark2_5-layer-inputs.patch` | required for the draft to load at all |\n| `spark-eagle3-v6.gguf`, `v6/…` | previous release, kept for existing links |\n| `spark-eagle3-v5.gguf`, root `model.safetensors`/`config.json` | first release, kept |\n\nTo rebuild the GGUF from the safetensors (needs a local copy of the Spark config and tokenizer, which the converter reads but does not instantiate):\n\n```bash\npython3 convert_hf_to_gguf.py v8 --target-model-dir /path/to/Spark-X2.6-4B \\\n    --outfile spark-eagle3-v8.gguf --outtype bf16\n```\n\n## [](#license) License\n\nApache-2.0, following the base model. Training data: codeparrot-clean (permissively licensed GitHub Python), Magicoder OSS-Instruct (MIT), UltraChat-200k (MIT), WikiText-103 (CC BY-SA 3\\.0) — the last is share-alike, which is worth knowing if you redistribute this commercially.\n\n## [](#citation) Citation\n\nIf this is useful, cite the EAGLE-3 paper for the architecture (Li et al., 2025) and link back here for the weights.\n\n**Downloads last month**\n: 1,056\n\nSafetensors[](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors)\n\nModel size\n\n0\\.2B params\n\nTensor type\n\nI64\n\n·\n\nF32\n\n·\n\nFiles info\n\nInference Providers [NEW](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers)\n\nThis model isn't deployed by any Inference Provider. Spark-X2.5-4B 的\"赛博治疗\"第一针：**部分有效，未根治**。本卡如实披露所有缺陷，请按需取用。 方法论致敬 [nerkyor 的 Qwen3.8-27B EfficientThink 系列](https://huggingface.co/nerkyor)。\n\n## [](#⚠️-先看缺陷（实测结论，2026-10-10）) ⚠️ 先看缺陷（实测结论，2026-10-10）\n\n- **长任务规划仍然死循环**：让它写一个飞机大战游戏，思考 8-10 分钟后**一个字正文都写不出来**——长链规划的病灶未治好\n\n- **治好的只是**：快问快答、极简单任务（脏上下文下 2 秒调工具）、真实会话中的部分重病例（见下表）\n\n- 验收重放的 19 例中 **12 例功能治愈、5-7 例残留长思考**；v2（加大剂量+DPO）尝试反而方差回退，已弃用\n\n- **结论：这是一个\"部分缓解\"的实验版本，不是成品**。生产使用请自行评估，欢迎在它基础上继续调教\n\n## [](#治了什么（背景）) 治了什么（背景）\n\n原版 Spark-X2.5-4B 在真实 harness 长会话中：单回合思考 30K+ token、烧 550+ 秒、撞 32K 上限后零正文输出。干净指令正常、脏上下文爆炸。\n\n本模型用 19 个真实 agent 会话病灶 \\+ 教师模型（Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B）重做轨迹，小剂量 SFT（LoRA r32，56 样本，3 epoch）训练。\n\n## [](#验收数据（19-个真实病灶重放，完整披露）) 验收数据（19 个真实病灶重放，完整披露）\n\n| 病例类型 | 原版 | 治疗版 | 判定 |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 重度（566s/32K输出/零正文） | 549-570s | **4-25s** | ✅ 12/19 治愈 |\n| 平均回合耗时 | 249s | 67s (3.7x) | 部分 |\n| 脏上下文+读图指令 | — | 2\\.2s 秒调工具 | ✅ |\n| **长任务规划（写飞机大战）** | 死循环 | **仍死循环（8-10min 零输出）** | ❌ 未治 |\n| 严格死循环 | 常见 | 重放中 0，**新任务仍会触发** | ⚠️ 部分 |\n\n## [](#已知失败原因（供接手者参考）) 已知失败原因（供接手者参考）\n\n- 训练序列被限制在 3K token（Windows TDR 看门狗掐杀长 kernel），**最长的重病灶样本没进训练集**——长任务死循环的病根没吃到药\n\n- 56 样本的小剂量对\"长程规划\"这种深层行为改变不足\n\n- 下一步：TdrDelay 注册表解锁 8K 序列 \\+ DPO 偏好对（数据已备好），或以此为底座继续调\n\n## [](#使用) 使用\n\n```\nllama-server -m spark-therapy-q8_0.gguf --jinja -ngl 99 -c 65536 -fa on --temp 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20\n```\n\n需要支持 `spark2_5` 架构的 llama.cpp（2026-10 后主线）。Q8\\_0 单档，低比特未验证（可能复发死循环）。\n\n## [](#致谢) 致谢\n\n- [](#betterwright-4b) BetterWright-4b\n\n**BetterWright-4b** is a full-parameter fine-tune of [XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B](https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B) specialised for driving a real browser through [BetterWright](https://github.com/BetterWright/betterwright) (a persistent, policy-guarded Playwright browser for AI agents). It is trained on execution-verified trajectories recorded from BetterWright's own `exec` agent loop on live websites, with short, decision-focused reasoning so long browsing sessions stay cheap and coherent.\n\n- Architecture: Spark-X2.5 hybrid attention (3 sliding-window layers per full-attention layer, window 512), 4B parameters, native 1M-token position range. Recommended serving window: **262,144 tokens**.\n\n- Tool format: the Spark-X2.5 chat template (`<tool_call>name<arg_key>k</arg_key><arg_value>v</arg_value></tool_call>`), thinking in `<think>…</think>`. Serve with SGLang `--tool-call-parser spark25 --reasoning-parser qwen3` or vLLM with the Spark plugin.\n\n- Target harness: `betterwright exec` / the interactive `betterwright` console (tools `browser`, `done`, plus `login`/`ask`/`handoff` when the host exposes them). It also works from the BetterWright MCP server and the Pi extension, which share the same `browser(code, note)` tool shape.\n\n## [](#benchmark-vs-the-base-model) Benchmark vs the base model\n\n| Metric (40 frozen holdout tasks: 30 Online-Mind2Web \\+ 10 Odysseys) | Spark-X2.5-4B (base) | BetterWright-4b |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Judge pass rate (score ≥ 8) | 2% | 5% |\n| Judge mean score (0–10) | 1\\.21 | 2\\.40 |\n| Answer grounded in observations | 22% | 40% |\n| Finished via `done`/`finalAnswer` (harness ok) | 22% | 18% |\n| Mean browser steps per task | 60\\.9 | 37\\.1 |\n| Mean output tokens per task | 21,067 | 14,810 |\n| Mean reasoning tokens per task | 11,495 | 3,140 |\n| Mean wall-clock per task (s) | 1,067 | 1,165 |\n\n| Per benchmark: judge pass rate | Base | BetterWright-4b |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Online-Mind2Web subset (n=30) | 3% | 7% |\n| Odysseys subset (n=10) | 0% | 0% |\n\nJudge: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 (via HF Inference Providers). Base reasons: {\"answered\": 7, \"done\": 2, \"max\\_tokens\": 3, \"stopped\": 3, \"timeout\": 25}. Tuned reasons: {\"done\": 7, \"error\": 2, \"max\\_tokens\": 5, \"stopped\": 1, \"timeout\": 25}.\n\nEvaluation protocol: identical prompts, identical BetterWright `exec` harness (headless BetterChromium, no vault, text-only observations, `--no-sandbox`), identical budgets (20 min wall-clock and 8,192 max output tokens per turn for Online-Mind2Web tasks, 40 min for Odysseys tasks), both models served with SGLang on the same GPU at the same time and run on the live web on 2026-09-03. Verdicts come from a strict text-only LLM judge (Kimi-K2.6 via HF Inference Providers) that only credits requirements evidenced in the browser observations; \"harness ok\" is BetterWright's own completion signal (`done` / `finalAnswer`). The tasks are a frozen holdout of 30 Online-Mind2Web (2025-11-23 snapshot) and 10 Odysseys tasks excluded from all training data. These are local judgments on a live web, not official leaderboard scores, and the sample is small; treat the deltas as directional.\n\n### [](#reading-these-numbers-honestly) Reading these numbers honestly\n\n- **What improved.** The judge's mean score doubled (1.21 \\-\\> 2\\.40), the share of final answers grounded in what the browser actually showed nearly doubled (22% \\-\\> 40%), reasoning tokens per task fell by 73% and total output tokens by 30%, and the model reaches an answer in \\~40% fewer browser steps. On the Online-Mind2Web subset the mean score went from 1\\.21 to 2\\.78 with half of the answers grounded.\n\n- **What did not.** The strict pass rate (score \\>= 8) moved from 1/40 to 2/40, which is within noise on 40 tasks. Both models still time out on most tasks: these are hard, long-horizon tasks on the live web, run under a wall-clock budget by a 4B model.\n\n- **A known handicap in this run.** Both models shared one GPU during the eval, and the tuned model's server received the worse share: its median model latency per turn was 14\\.2 s against 7\\.8 s for the base, with similar output length per turn. At 30-50 steps per task that gap consumed a large part of the 20-minute budget. Inspection of the timed-out tuned trajectories shows steady progress (2-11 distinct pages, no action repeated more than 3 times), not loops. A re-run with the tuned model served alone and a step budget instead of a wall clock is the first item of the v1.1 evaluation and will be added here.\n\n- **Base-model behaviour the training removed.** The base model's \"answered\" finishes were mostly unsupported claims (its judge pass rate was 5% in a first baseline run and 2\\.5% in this one); the tuned model ends tasks through the `done` tool with grounded answers or keeps working.\n\n- **What is next (v1.1).** Rejection-sampling on the model's own rollouts (\\~950 additional judged trajectories were collected overnight), a longer-horizon eval, and a preference-optimisation pass on judged pairs.\n\n## [](#how-to-use) How to use\n\n### [](#serve-sglang) Serve (SGLang)\n\n```bash\ndocker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host -p 30000:30000 \\\n  -v /path/to/BetterWright-4b:/model:ro \\\n  lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260827-20621aa1 \\\n  python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model --served-model-name betterwright-4b \\\n    --tool-call-parser spark25 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --trust-remote-code \\\n    --context-length 262144 --chat-template /model/chat_template.jinja --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000\n```\n\n### [](#drive-a-browser-with-betterwright) Drive a browser with BetterWright\n\n```bash\nnpm install -g betterwright && betterwright setup\nbetterwright exec \"find the top Hacker News story and give me its title and points\" \\\n  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --model betterwright-4b\n# interactive console with the same model\nbetterwright --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --model betterwright-4b\n```\n\nSampling: temperature 1\\.0, top\\_p 0\\.95 (the base model's defaults) work well; the model finishes read-only tasks by returning `{ finalAnswer }` from the last `browser` call when it can.\n\n### [](#transformers) Transformers\n\nThe repository ships `modeling_spark.py` with attention dispatch added, so `attn_implementation=\"sdpa\"`, `\"flex_attention\"` and `\"flash_attention_2\"` work in addition to eager (transformers ≥ 4\\.57; the tied-weights and mask-builder differences of transformers 5\\.x are handled).\n\n```python\nfrom transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer\ntok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(\"ProCreations/BetterWright-4b\", trust_remote_code=True)\nmodel = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\"ProCreations/BetterWright-4b\", trust_remote_code=True,\n                                             dtype=\"bfloat16\", attn_implementation=\"sdpa\").cuda()\n```\n\n## [](#training) Training\n\n- Base: `XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B`, full-parameter SFT (all 4B weights), bf16 weights with stochastic-rounding 8-bit AdamW (torchao), FlexAttention with sliding-window block masks, gradient checkpointing, single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB).\n\n- Data: 502 execution-verified BetterWright `exec` trajectories on the live web (teachers: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), kept only when a strict LLM judge scored them ≥ 7/10 from the browser observations; per-turn reasoning rewritten into compact rationales (typically 15–120 words). Tasks: Online-Mind2Web and Odysseys tasks outside the frozen holdout, plus \\~1,000 synthetic tasks over \\~330 real sites and sandbox/demo sites.\n\n- Samples: 2182 training sequences (33,400,315 tokens, 5,384,477 supervised tokens; max 97,693 tokens). Whole-trajectory sequences supervise every assistant turn, keeping compact reasoning on \\~50% of turns (always the last) and masking the empty-think marker on the rest so the model never learns to skip thinking; extra \"deep-turn\" samples train single late turns on inference-format history. 898 general-assistant replay samples (no\\_robots prompts answered with compact reasoning) are mixed in.\n\n- Schedule: 122 optimizer steps of \\~262,144 tokens, peak LR 8e-6 with 20 warmup steps and cosine decay to 10%, weight decay 0, grad clip 1\\.0; 145\\.2 minutes wall-clock; final validation loss 0\\.7382 (first eval 0\\.763).\n\n- Context: trained on sequences up to 96k tokens; the architecture's native positions extend to 1M. Recommended serving window 262k.\n\n## [](#limitations) Limitations\n\n- Text-only: the model never sees screenshots; it relies on BetterWright's accessibility snapshots, DOM text and JSON results. Proof screenshots are still captured for the human.\n\n- Trained on public, login-free sites and on sandbox/demo sites for write actions (carts, forms, fake checkouts); it has not been trained on authenticated flows with real credentials.\n\n- The judge used for filtering and evaluation is an LLM, not human review; live sites change, so re-running the benchmark will not reproduce identical numbers.\n\n- 4B parameters: strong at operating the browser, weaker than large models at open-ended reasoning about page content.\n\n## [](#acknowledgements) Acknowledgements\n\nBase model by XHToken (Spark-X2.5-4B, Apache-2.0). Harness, benchmarks and browser: The BetterWright Project (MIT). Task sources: Online-Mind2Web (OSU NLP) and Odysseys (Jang et al., 2026, MIT-licensed task data). Teacher for trajectory generation and judging: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next served locally with SGLang.\n\n**Downloads last month**\n: 170\n\nSafetensors[](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors)\n\nModel size\n\n4B params\n\nTensor type\n\nBF16\n\n·\n\nChat template\n\nFiles info\n\nInference Providers [NEW](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers)\n\n[](/tasks/text-generation \"Learn more about text-generation\")\n\nText Generation\n\nThis model isn't deployed by any Inference Provider. [](#spark-x26-4b-with-a-causal-encoder-decoder-ced-split-experimental-retrofit) Spark-X2.6-4B with a Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) split: experimental retrofit\n\n## [](#update-2026-10-29-v2-split-moved-from-layer-18-to-layer-24-recommended) Update 2026-10-29: v2, split moved from layer 18 to layer 24 (recommended)\n\nv1 lost a lot of long-context retrieval. The reason turned out to be the split point: the decoder's global layers (23, 27) need information that the layer-18 state simply doesn't contain yet (a closed-form fit from H\\_18 to the original layer-23/27 values leaves 37-48% error, and no projector training fixed it; from H\\_24 it's 6%). v2 moves the split to layer 24: layers 0-23 = encoder (all original weights, including global layer 23), layers 24-35 = decoder, whose 3 global layers (27, 31, 35) read K/V projected from RMSNorm(H\\_24).\n\n**v2 is not trained at all.** The 6 projection matrices are a closed-form ridge-regression fit of the original model's K/V from H\\_24 (about 0\\.5M tokens of PG19 / code / chat / synthetic retrieval); there is no LoRA and every other weight is the original.\n\n|  | v1 (split 18, trained) | **v2 (split 24, no training)** | original |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| long-context generation, 138 items, official scorers: RULER (multi-key needles \\+ variable tracking) | 69% | **88%** | 90% |\n| NoLiMa (36 items) | 8% | **31%** | 33% |\n| BABILong qa1-3 (54 items) | **52%** | 43% | 50% |\n| all 138 | 47% | **55%** | 59% |\n| KL(original ‖ CED), last 512 of 8K, replay 1024 (PG19 / code / chat, 85 held-out seqs) | 0\\.066 / 0\\.095 / 0\\.105 | **0\\.040 / 0\\.083 / 0\\.052** | 0 |\n| top-1 agreement with the original | 0\\.885 / 0\\.922 / 0\\.889 | **0\\.896 / 0\\.937 / 0\\.913** | 1 |\n| needles with 4 near-duplicate distractors, 20 trials at 4K / 8K / 16K | 19 / 18 / 20 | **20 / 20 / 20** | 20 / 20 / 20 |\n| GSM8K, 100 questions, greedy | **87** | 85 | 89 |\n| prefill speedup vs original, PyTorch reference path, replay 1024, 4K / 8K / 16K | **1\\.52 / 1\\.67 / 1\\.72x** | 1\\.35 / 1\\.42 / 1\\.46x | 1x |\n\nThe trade: more of the model runs over the whole prompt (24 of 36 layers instead of 18), so prefill saves about a third instead of about half; in exchange retrieval comes most of the way back to the original. Decode speed is the same as the original either way. Long-context items are thinking-off, greedy, up to 32K tokens; RULER variable tracking is included with the answer prefix pre-filled as in the official setup. llama.cpp prefill on an Intel Arc Pro B70 (Vulkan, Q4\\_K\\_M, llama-server two-phase prefill with replay 1024, ub 512, warm; prompt of repeated token ids, timing only), tokens/s at 4K / 8K / 16K / 32K: original 2867 / 2503 / 1942 / 1332, v1 4234 / 4147 / 3535 / 2595 (1.48 / 1\\.66 / 1\\.82 / 1\\.95x), **v2 3616 / 3358 / 2710 / 1907 (1.26 / 1\\.34 / 1\\.40 / 1\\.43x)**. The PyTorch speedups in the table use the same reference implementation for all variants (the GGUF parity is: mean KL 3\\.5e-4 to 2\\.3e-3 vs the PyTorch path, within about 2x of the plain-GGUF-vs-PyTorch noise floor on the same sequences).\n\n**v2 files:** `spark-ced24-Q8_0.gguf`, `spark-ced24-Q4_K_M.gguf` (GGUF key `spark2_5.ced.split` = 24, same llama.cpp patch as v1, same bartowski imatrix), `ced_weights_split24.safetensors` (the 6 projections, bf16, 31 MB; `demo.py` reads the split from the file). The v1 files below are unchanged.\n\n---\n\n# [](#v1-2026-10-26-split-at-layer-18-trained) v1 (2026-10-26): split at layer 18, trained\n\n> Experimental research artifact, not a drop-in model. Runs in PyTorch (`demo.py`) and in a llama.cpp fork (GGUFs below); stock llama.cpp and vLLM cannot load it.\n\nThis takes the finished [XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B](https://huggingface.co/XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B) (36 layers, sliding-window layers with a global-attention layer every 4th layer) and converts it to the **CED layout of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** ([arXiv 2609\\.19969](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19969), sec. 2\\.2 and 3\\.2.2) *without pre-training anything from scratch*:\n\n- layers 0-17 = **causal encoder** (layers 0-13 are the original weights, 14-17 carry a small LoRA), layers 18-35 = **decoder**;\n\n- the global-attention K/V of the 5 decoder global layers (19, 23, 27, 31, 35) are **projected from the encoder's last hidden state** with layer-dependent weights instead of from each layer's own hidden state: C\\_l = RMSNorm(H\\_18) W\\_l (the paper writes C\\_l = H\\_{L/2} W\\_l; the gain-free RMSNorm on the input is my addition so the projections can be initialised from the layers' own weights);\n\n- decoder sliding-window K/V stay layer-wise and are rebuilt by **bounded replay** of the last prompt tokens.\n\nPrefill runs the encoder (18 layers) over the whole prompt and the decoder (18 layers) over only the last `replay` tokens: close to half the prefill compute. Decode compute and the KV-cache size are unchanged (exact CED keeps one cache per layer; KV compression is CSA2's job, not CED's).\n\n## [](#what-was-trained) What was trained\n\nOnly a small number of weights, by distillation against the original model (KL on its own logits \\+ normalised per-layer hidden-state MSE; no labels, no teacher other than Spark itself), about 50M training tokens in total on one local B70 (\\~6 h):\n\n1. closed-form ridge init of the 10 new K/V projections (5 layers x K,V, 26M parameters) from H\\_18 onto the original layers' K/V;\n\n2. training of those projections;\n\n3.\n\n   - LoRA (rank 16) on all 18 decoder layers;\n\n4.\n\n   - LoRA (rank 16) on encoder layers 14-17 (data: PG19 books, GitHub code, WildChat);\n\n5.\n\n   - 300 more steps with the original model's own sampled answers to GSM8K-train questions and general prompts mixed in (each conversation as its own sequence, full replay).\n\nEncoder layers 0-13 are bit-identical to the original. The LoRA can be folded into the weights (`Spark.merge_lora`), after which decode runs at the original's speed.\n\n## [](#quality-distillation-fidelity) Quality: distillation fidelity\n\n85 held-out 8192-token sequences (44 PG19, 24 code, 17 chat) never used for training or for choosing a checkpoint. KL(original \\|\\| CED) on the last 512 positions, lower is better:\n\n| variant | PG19 (replay 1024) | code | chat | PG19 (replay 512) | code | chat |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| naive init (the layers' own K/V weights on H\\_18) | 0\\.922 | 1\\.613 | 0\\.967 | 0\\.960 | 1\\.716 | 1\\.060 |\n| closed-form ridge init | 0\\.214 | 0\\.492 | 0\\.301 | 0\\.269 | 0\\.561 | 0\\.387 |\n| \\+ trained K/V projections (26M) | 0\\.087 | 0\\.144 | 0\\.134 | 0\\.124 | 0\\.177 | 0\\.187 |\n| \\+ LoRA on the 18 decoder layers | 0\\.076 | 0\\.121 | 0\\.118 | 0\\.105 | 0\\.148 | 0\\.159 |\n| **final: \\+ LoRA on encoder layers 14-17, \\+ on-policy math/chat data** | 0\\.066 | 0\\.095 | 0\\.105 | 0\\.093 | 0\\.122 | 0\\.141 |\n| *floor: original K/V in the decoder, replay only* | 0\\.000 | 0\\.000 | 0\\.000 | 0\\.046 | 0\\.056 | 0\\.077 |\n\n- **Replay of 1024 tokens (2x the 512 window) is lossless** (KL 0\\.000 on top of the K/V approximation); the paper-style replay of exactly one window (512) costs 0\\.05-0.08 KL by itself. Use `replay=1024`.\n\n- Cross-entropy on the last 1024 tokens, original \\-\\> CED (PG19 / code / chat): 2\\.676 \\-\\> 2\\.705 / 0\\.961 \\-\\> 0\\.993 / 2\\.089 \\-\\> 2\\.017. Top-1 agreement with the original: 0\\.885 / 0\\.922 / 0\\.889.\n\n### [](#next-to-ordinary-quantization) Next to ordinary quantization\n\nKL to the unquantized model for the usual GGUF quants ([bartowski](https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Spark-X2.6-4B-GGUF) imatrix quants vs his bf16 GGUF, llama.cpp `--kl-divergence` on CPU, 4K-token chunks, same text domains) next to CED. Not the same positions as the CED numbers (CED: last 512 of 8K sequences), so read it as a rough placement:\n\n|  | PG19 | code | chat | mean |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Q8\\_0 (GGUF, 4\\.38 GB) | 0\\.003 | 0\\.001 | 0\\.001 | 0\\.002 |\n| Q6\\_K (GGUF, 3\\.61 GB) | 0\\.008 | 0\\.002 | 0\\.003 | 0\\.004 |\n| Q5\\_K\\_M (GGUF, 3\\.16 GB) | 0\\.024 | 0\\.010 | 0\\.009 | 0\\.014 |\n| Q4\\_K\\_M (GGUF, 2\\.62 GB) | 0\\.070 | 0\\.027 | 0\\.035 | 0\\.044 |\n| IQ4\\_XS (GGUF, 2\\.34 GB) | 0\\.112 | 0\\.039 | 0\\.049 | 0\\.067 |\n| **CED (this repo)** | **0\\.066** | **0\\.095** | **0\\.105** | **0\\.089** |\n| IQ3\\_M (GGUF, 2\\.23 GB) | 0\\.248 | 0\\.096 | 0\\.104 | 0\\.149 |\n| Q3\\_K\\_M (GGUF, 1\\.99 GB) | 0\\.302 | 0\\.117 | 0\\.156 | 0\\.192 |\n| Q2\\_K (GGUF, 1\\.61 GB) | 0\\.912 | 0\\.420 | 0\\.617 | 0\\.650 |\n| IQ2\\_M (GGUF, 1\\.57 GB) | 0\\.871 | 0\\.482 | 0\\.597 | 0\\.650 |\n\nCED costs about as much as an IQ4\\_XS-to-IQ3\\_M quant. It saves prefill compute, not memory, and the two should stack (errors add up).\n\n### [](#task-check-gsm8k-100-questions) Task check: GSM8K, 100 questions\n\nGreedy, chat template, no thinking, the same PyTorch code path for both: original **89/100**, CED **87/100** (6 questions only the original solved, 4 only CED). A 2-question gap on 100 is within noise.\n\n## [](#speed-same-reference-implementation-for-both-bf16-lora-merged-steady-state-median-intel-arc-pro-b70) Speed (same reference implementation for both, bf16, LoRA merged, steady-state median, Intel Arc Pro B70)\n\nPrefill:\n\n| prompt tokens | original | CED, replay 512 | CED, replay 1024 |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 4,096 | 0\\.59 s | 0\\.35 s (1.67x) | 0\\.39 s (1.52x) |\n| 8,192 | 1\\.27 s | 0\\.73 s (1.75x) | 0\\.76 s (1.67x) |\n| 16,384 | 3\\.20 s | 1\\.73 s (1.85x) | 1\\.86 s (1.72x) |\n\nThe reference implementation is plain PyTorch with chunked attention, so absolute tokens/s are not comparable with optimised engines; the ratio is what carries over. The asymptote is \\~2x. Decode at 8K context: original 52\\.4 ms/token, CED 52\\.9 ms/token (LoRA merged). CED is a prefill optimisation, not a decode one.\n\n### [](#retrieval-needle-in-a-haystack-with-4-near-duplicate-distractors-20-trials-per-length-greedy) Retrieval (\"needle in a haystack\" with 4 near-duplicate distractors, 20 trials per length, greedy)\n\n| prompt tokens | original | CED (replay 512) | CED (replay 1024) |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 4,096 | 20/20 | 19/20 | 19/20 |\n| 8,192 | 20/20 | 18/20 | 18/20 |\n| 16,384 | 20/20 | 20/20 | 20/20 |\n\n## [](#llamacpp-gguf) llama.cpp (GGUF)\n\n`spark-ced-Q8_0.gguf` (4.4 GB) and `spark-ced-Q4_K_M.gguf` (2.6 GB) have the LoRA merged in and carry the 10 K/V projections as extra tensors (`blk.N.ced_k`, `ced_v`; GGUF key `spark2_5.ced.split`). They need llama.cpp with the CED patch (`llama.cpp-ced.patch` in this repo, against upstream commit `a0e6dc738`; `git apply` it and build as usual, e.g. `-DGGML_CUDA=ON` or `-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`); stock llama.cpp refuses to load them (tensor-count error). The patch adds the CED graph, the converter and a `llama_set_ced` API and does nothing for models without CED tensors. `llama-server -np 1` does the two-phase prefill by itself (replay 1024, `LLAMA_CED_REPLAY=0` turns it off); other slot counts fall back to normal prefill. The quants use bartowski's imatrix, not one of my own.\n\nLogits match the PyTorch CED within the bf16 noise floor (mean KL 3e-4 to 8e-4, CPU and Vulkan); with the decoder sliding-window mask deliberately removed the same test shows KL 0\\.34, so it does catch a broken graph. KL to the *original* bf16 GGUF (mean over PG19 / code / chat, llama.cpp `--kl-divergence`): CED bf16 0\\.067, CED Q8\\_0 0\\.068, CED Q4\\_K\\_M 0\\.114 (plain Q4\\_K\\_M: 0\\.044).\n\nPrefill, tokens/s, Q4\\_K\\_M, warm, ub 512, `-ngl 99`, stock = XHToken's official Q4\\_K\\_M:\n\n| prompt tokens | RTX 4090 stock | RTX 4090 CED |  | Arc Pro B70 (Vulkan) stock | B70 CED |  |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 4,096 | 18\\.1k | 24\\.3k | 1\\.34x | 3\\.0k | 4\\.4k | 1\\.46x |\n| 8,192 |  |  |  | 2\\.6k | 4\\.2k | 1\\.66x |\n| 16,384 |  |  |  | 2\\.0k | 3\\.5k | 1\\.80x |\n| 32,768 | 14\\.4k | 23\\.4k | 1\\.62x | 1\\.3k | 2\\.6k | 1\\.93x |\n| 131,072 | 8\\.7k | 14\\.7k | 1\\.68x |  |  |  |\n| 262,144 | 5\\.7k | 8\\.3k | 1\\.45x |  |  |  |\n\nDecode (4090, tok/s at 4K / 32K / 128K context): stock 219 / 175 / 93, CED 226 / 177 / 94\\. The 4090 numbers are from a rented host with an i9-14900K; an earlier run on a slow server CPU was CPU-bound (GPU 48-64% busy) and showed almost no gain, so prefill speedups on a weak host will be smaller. The B70 numbers were measured on a build that also has my own Intel Xe2 Vulkan kernel changes (not in the patch here); the stock column is the same build without CED, so the ratio is CED's.\n\n## [](#usage) Usage\n\n```\npython demo.py /path/to/Spark-X2.6-4B ced_weights.safetensors --replay 1024 --compare\n```\n\n`spark_ced.py` is a self-contained PyTorch re-implementation of Spark (checked against the reference code and an fp32 CPU run) with the CED path. `ced_weights.safetensors` holds the 10 K/V projections and the LoRA deltas (bf16, 89 MB); the base weights come from the original repo. In code: `proj, lora = load_ced_weights(...)`, `S.merge_lora(lora)`, then `S.ced_prefill(ids, proj, caches, tail=1024)` and `S.ced_step(...)` with `lora=None`.\n\n## [](#caveats) Caveats\n\n- Not an official or endorsed variant of Spark or DeepSeek; the architecture is from the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash paper.\n\n- The paper trains CED from scratch with a jointly trained encoder; this retrofit adapts a finished model with LoRA and distillation, so it is lossy (see tables). Greedy outputs diverge from the original after a few dozen tokens; a multi-step arithmetic prompt can come out wrong where the original is right.\n\n- Evaluation is distillation fidelity (KL/CE), 100 GSM8K questions and a synthetic retrieval test, not task benchmarks. The PyTorch speed table above comes from a reference implementation, not an inference engine; the llama.cpp numbers are above.\n\n- GGUF speed numbers use a prompt of repeated token ids (timing only; quality is measured separately); the server path has been checked for identical greedy output on CPU only.\n\n- CED GGUF Q4\\_K\\_M is noticeably lossier than plain Q4\\_K\\_M (KL 0\\.114 vs 0\\.044); Q8\\_0 adds nothing on top of CED.\n\n## [](#credits) Credits\n\nMade by [@imdariotoo](https://x.com/imdariotoo). [Expand in Data Studio](/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6/viewer/default/train)\n\n---\n\n- [ Previous]()\n\n- [1](/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6/viewer/default/train?p=0)\n\n- [2](/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6/viewer/default/train?p=1)\n\n- [3](/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6/viewer/default/train?p=2)\n\n- [...](#)\n\n- [100](/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6/viewer/default/train?p=99)\n\n- [Next](/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6/viewer/default/train?p=1)\n\n- [What v1.6 adds](#what-v16-adds \"What v1.6 adds\")\n\n  - [Verification that catches something](#verification-that-catches-something \"Verification that catches something\")\n\n  - [Difficulty, and traces that scale with it](#difficulty-and-traces-that-scale-with-it \"Difficulty, and traces that scale with it\")\n\n  - [Harness prompts on half the corpus](#harness-prompts-on-half-the-corpus \"Harness prompts on half the corpus\")\n\n- [Composition](#composition \"Composition\")\n\n- [Token statistics](#token-statistics \"Token statistics\")\n\n- [Load](#load \"Load\")\n\n- [Format for Qwen3.8 training](#format-for-qwen38-training \"Format for Qwen3.8 training\")\n\n- [Notes](#notes \"Notes\")\n\n- [Provenance](#provenance \"Provenance\")\n\n  - [Release chain](#release-chain \"Release chain\")\n\n- [License](#license \"License\")\n\n# [](#sriq-sft-v16) sriq-sft-v1.6\n\nShareGPT-compatible supervised fine-tuning conversations by [SRIQ](https://sriq.org). Questions are generated in 30 languages. Assistant targets contain compressed Simplified Chinese reasoning followed by the original final answer. The final answer is not rewritten by the compression step.\n\n|  |  |\n| --- | --- |\n| **Rows** | 9,988 |\n| **Languages** | 30 |\n| **Turns** | system, human, gpt |\n| **Reasoning** | compressed Simplified Chinese inside `<think>` tags |\n| **Verification** | 19\\.5% of traces catch a real mistake and repair it |\n| **Difficulty** | easy / medium / hard, with trace length scaled to match |\n| **Previous version** | [sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.5) |\n\n- `conversations`: a system turn, a human turn, then one GPT turn.\n\n- System turn: `from` is `system`; `value` contains either a short generic preamble or a long synthetic coding-harness preamble.\n\n- Human turn: `from` is `human`; `value` contains the question.\n\n- GPT turn: `from` is `gpt`; `value` contains `<think>Chinese reasoning</think>` followed by the final answer.\n\n- Extra columns: `topic`, `difficulty`, `language` (the requested question language), and `verification` (new in v1.6).\n\nThere are no rejected responses in the SFT export.\n\n## [](#what-v16-adds) What v1.6 adds\n\n### [](#verification-that-catches-something) Verification that catches something\n\nThrough v1.5 the verification step could only ever agree with itself. The compressed trace is rewritten from a chain of thought that already produced the final answer, so the check at the end had nothing to find: **0\\.9%** of v1.5 traces caught a mistake, and 546 closed on an explicit 答案对. A model trained on that learns the shape of checking without the function — the first adapter trained on v1.5 reached the right answer on IMO 1990 P3 through steps containing `p | p-1`, which holds for no prime, and stamped it correct.\n\nA share of v1.6 rows are generated down a second path: one step of the reasoning is deliberately wrong, and the verification catches it, names it and redoes it. The final answer is the original correct one either way.\n\n| `verification` | Rows | Share |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `correct` — the check found a real mistake and repaired it | 1,951 | **19\\.5%** |\n| `confirm` — the check ran and found nothing | 8,037 | 80\\.5% |\n\nA row is rejected and regenerated unless the planted mistake appears verbatim in the trace, and unless the trace stops short of announcing it before the check. A trace that merely claims to have verified something is the thing being fixed.\n\n### [](#difficulty-and-traces-that-scale-with-it) Difficulty, and traces that scale with it\n\nEvery row in v1.3 through v1.5 was `difficulty: hard`, so nothing in the corpus taught a model that a cheap question deserves a cheap answer. v1.6 samples all three and gives the compression step a length budget per difficulty.\n\n| Difficulty | Rows | Median reasoning tokens |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| easy | 1,872 | **25** |\n| medium | 2,648 | 140 |\n| hard | 5,468 | 254 |\n\nFor comparison, v1.5 spent a median of 349 reasoning tokens on everything, because everything was hard. An easy question in v1.6 costs about a fourteenth of that.\n\n### [](#harness-prompts-on-half-the-corpus) Harness prompts on half the corpus\n\nModels fine-tuned on a corpus of short system prompts hold Chinese reasoning under a short system prompt, and drift back to English behind a real agent harness. Half of v1.6 carries a synthetic coding-harness preamble — persona line, guidelines, a `# Skills` listing, project context, an environment footer — so the behaviour is trained where it otherwise collapses.\n\n| System prompt | Rows |\n| --- | --- |\n| `You are a helpful assistant` | 4,988 |\n| Synthetic coding-harness preamble | 5,000 |\n\nHarness preambles run to a median of 1,005 tokens and a maximum of 1,933. The user turn is still an ordinary question, not a tool-call trace: the preamble is distractor context, and the target is that the model keeps reasoning in Chinese and answering in the question's language despite it.\n\n## [](#composition) Composition\n\n| Axis | Split |\n| --- | --- |\n| Topic | math 6,081 (60.9%) · coding 3,907 (39.1%) |\n| Difficulty | hard 5,468 · medium 2,648 · easy 1,872 |\n| Verification | confirm 8,037 · correct 1,951 |\n| Languages | 30, between 295 and 390 rows each |\n\nArabic, Bengali, Czech, Dutch, English, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tamil, Thai, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu, Vietnamese.\n\n## [](#token-statistics) Token statistics\n\nCounts use `tiktoken` `cl100k_base`, not the training model's tokenizer.\n\n| Slice | Total tokens |\n| --- | --- |\n| System prompts | 5,192,983 |\n| Reasoning | 2,312,789 |\n| Final answer | 13,082,224 |\n| Reasoning \\+ final answer, including think tags | 15,445,506 |\n\n## [](#load) Load\n\n```python\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\n\ndataset = load_dataset(\"sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6\", split=\"train\")\nconversation = dataset[0][\"conversations\"]\n```\n\n## [](#format-for-qwen38-training) Format for Qwen3.8 training\n\nThe export uses standard ShareGPT fields. Qwen3.8's native template expects reasoning in a separate field, so convert the record before applying that template:\n\n```python\nfrom transformers import AutoTokenizer\n\nsystem, question = conversation[0][\"value\"], conversation[1][\"value\"]\nresponse = conversation[2][\"value\"]\nreasoning, answer = response.removeprefix(\"<think>\").split(\"</think>\", 1)\nmessages = [\n    {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": system},\n    {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": question},\n    {\"role\": \"assistant\", \"reasoning_content\": reasoning, \"content\": answer.strip()},\n]\ntokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(\"Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B\")\ntext = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(\n    messages,\n    tokenize=False,\n    add_generation_prompt=False,\n    preserve_thinking=True,\n)\n```\n\nFor other models, adapt the ShareGPT roles and fields to the trainer's expected conversation schema while retaining the complete GPT `value`. Do not place the same reasoning in both `content` and `reasoning_content` for Qwen's template.\n\nFor SFT, include the assistant's reasoning and final answer in the loss and mask system/user/prompt tokens. Check that the rendered training text retains the Chinese reasoning and that the assistant loss mask covers it. Use the target tokenizer to check lengths and keep repeated questions in the same train/evaluation split.\n\nThe harness rows are long. Set the sequence length to keep them whole — truncating the preamble removes the signal those rows exist to teach. If you must cap, drop the row rather than truncate it.\n\n## [](#notes) Notes\n\n`verification` is a new column, so this dataset cannot be appended to a v1.5 repository; the schemas differ.\n\nNothing here is a benchmark result. The figures describe what the corpus contains, not measured gains from training on it.\n\n## [](#provenance) Provenance\n\n|  |  |\n| --- | --- |\n| **Data revision** | `fa9e48709631a7be4eae3e38252c3a26fff3c0f3` |\n| **Published** | 2026-09-20 22:31 UTC |\n| **Built with** | pipeline commit `661ca90` in [`sriq/sriq-sft`](https://git.nixre.dev/git/sriq/sriq-sft) |\n| **Previous** | [v1.5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.5) |\n| **Trained into** | [sriq-diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-v1.6](https://huggingface.co/sriq-ai/sriq-diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-v1.6) |\n\nThe card above may change; the parquet at that revision will not. Pin it when training, so the corpus is the one that was measured:\n\n```python\nload_dataset(\"sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6\", split=\"train\",\n             revision=\"fa9e48709631a7be4eae3e38252c3a26fff3c0f3\")\n```\n\n### [](#release-chain) Release chain\n\nEach version exists to close a defect in the one before it.\n\n| Version | Rows | Data revision | What it introduced | The defect it left behind |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| v1.3 | 2,703 | `84f74b6` | compressed Simplified Chinese reasoning, 30 languages | traces stop at the answer — 15\\.2% carry a `验` block, 0\\.3% end on an explicit judgement |\n| v1.4 | 825 | `be3a4b6` | a verification step closing the trace (95.4% carry `验`) | Chinese reasoning reverts to English behind a long agent-harness prompt |\n| v1.5 | 1,424 | `e7ee870` | long synthetic harness preambles on 599 of 1,424 rows | the check inherited from v1.4 could only ever agree — 0\\.9% caught a mistake |\n| **v1.6** | 9,988 | `fa9e487` | verification that catches a real planted mistake (19.5%), graded difficulty, a `verification` column | — current release |\n\nThe commits behind this release:\n\n| Commit | What it changed |\n| --- | --- |\n| `5d05bed` | the self-check generation path — one step deliberately wrong, the verification catches it |\n| `56d3517` | moved the compression prompts out of Python into `prompts/*.txt` |\n| `2a83270` | the prompt shows the target register as a worked before/after instead of describing it |\n| `b782b8f` | rejects rows that telegraph the planted mistake before the check; scales trace length to difficulty |\n| `759216c` | support for endpoints that cannot constrain decoding (no dataset effect) |\n| `661ca90` | compression measured on the trace rather than the whole response |\n\nOne more difference from v1.5, not attributable to a single commit: harness preambles here run to a median of 1,005 and a maximum of 1,933 tokens, against v1.5's median 1,518 and maximum 15,976, so the harness rows now fit inside a practical context cap.\n\n**The corpus is ordered, not shuffled.** Rows 0–4,987 carry the generic preamble and rows 4,988–9,987 carry the harness preamble, the same layout v1.5 had. A tail split therefore holds out nothing but harness rows, and a head split trains on none of them. Shuffle before splitting.\n\n## [](#license) License\n\nApache-2.0.\n\nCopy to bucket\n\nUse this dataset\n\n**Downloads last month**\n\n: 74\n\n[]()\n\nNumber of rows:\n\n9,988\n\n[]()\n\nTotal file size:\n\n83\\.3 MB\n\n## Models trained or fine-tuned on sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6\n\n[](/sriq-ai/SRIQ-MiniCPM5-2B-v1.6)\n\n![](https://cdn-avatars.huggingface.co/v1/production/uploads/69ccfe9d66dc2f65a558e917/MoYpZKNeScPZHJffQc2UO.png)\n\n#### sriq-ai/SRIQ-MiniCPM5-2B-v1.6\n\nText Generation • 3B • Updated Sep 26 • 269 • 1\n\n[](/sriq-ai/sriq-diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-v1.6)\n\n![](https://cdn-avatars.huggingface.co/v1/production/uploads/69ccfe9d66dc2f65a558e917/MoYpZKNeScPZHJffQc2UO.png)\n\n#### sriq-ai/sriq-diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-v1.6\n\nImage-Text-to-Text • 26B • Updated Sep 21 • 70\n\n[](/sriq-ai/sriq-mimo_v2.6-9b-v1.6)\n\n![](https://cdn-avatars.huggingface.co/v1/production/uploads/69ccfe9d66dc2f65a558e917/MoYpZKNeScPZHJffQc2UO.png)\n\n#### sriq-ai/sriq-mimo\\_v2.6-9b-v1.6\n\nImage-Text-to-Text • 10B • Updated Sep 25 • 65 • 1\n\n[](/sriq-ai/sriq-diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-v1.6-FP8-dynamic)\n\n![](https://cdn-avatars.huggingface.co/v1/production/uploads/69ccfe9d66dc2f65a558e917/MoYpZKNeScPZHJffQc2UO.png)\n\n#### sriq-ai/sriq-diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-v1.6-FP8-dynamic\n\nImage-Text-to-Text • 26B • Updated Sep 21 • 58\n\nSystem theme\n\nCompany\n\n[TOS](/terms-of-service) [Privacy](/privacy) [About](/huggingface) [Careers](https://apply.workable.com/huggingface/) [](/)\n\nWebsite\n\n[Models](/models) [Datasets](/datasets) [Spaces](/spaces) [Pricing](/pricing) [Docs](/docs)"

Each row asks for an object with switchable animations built only from procedural geometry. The assistant turn is a compressed Simplified Chinese reasoning trace inside `<think>` tags, followed by the answer. Same columns as [sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6), so the two concatenate.\n\n> **Growing dataset.** This repo will keep growing: new rows are added and existing ones updated over time. Row counts below describe the current upload; pin a `revision` in `load_dataset` for a fixed snapshot.\n\n## [](#contents) Contents\n\n| Source | Rows | Answer | easy / medium / hard | Median trace tokens | Median answer chars |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| three.js | 1,392 | one self-contained `.html` file (three.js from a CDN) | 348 / 616 / 428 | 5,335 | 40,713 |\n| OpenSCAD | 140 | one `.scad` file, animations driven by `$t` | 35 / 74 / 31 | 5,336 | 26,234 |\n| **Total** | **1,532** |  |  |  |  |\n\nToken counts use `cl100k_base`. The three.js rows come first, then the OpenSCAD rows.\n\n## [](#fields) Fields\n\n- `conversations`: system (`You are a helpful assistant`), human (the request), gpt (`<think>trace</think> answer`).\n\n- `topic`: always `spatial`. `language`: always `English` (the request language). `verification`: always `confirm`.\n\n- `difficulty`: requested structural complexity (simple → easy, moderate → medium, intricate → hard).\n\n## [](#how-it-was-built) How it was built\n\n1. **Seed.** An object and its animations are sampled from a pool of subjects crossed with era, region and scale.\n\n2. **Answer.** An undisclosed teacher model writes the answer. A second undisclosed model writes the trace from the finished code (the teacher's own reasoning is not available).\n\n3. **OpenSCAD rows** were rendered with the `openscad` CLI and rejected (or sent back to the teacher for repair) on any warning, error, or empty top-level object.\n\n4. **Dedup.** Near-duplicate objects in the three.js rows are dropped at export, keeping the earliest. The OpenSCAD rows are included in full.\n\n## [](#what-v19-changes-from-v18) What v1.9 changes from [v1.8](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-spatial-sft-v1.8)\n\nv1.8 had 250 three.js traces (17.5%) matching a refusal/meta pattern such as 「不能提供内部思维链。以下为基于成品的设计摘要。」. In v1.9 every source row whose trace matched (255 before dedup) was re-traced from its unchanged answer by `inception/mercury-3` via OpenRouter, under the current trace prompt and gates:\n\n- the answer must pass a headless-Chromium runtime check (all buttons clicked, no page or console errors);\n\n- the trace must be mostly Chinese, contain no pasted code, contain no refusal/meta text, have a `验：` step naming an identifier in the code, and quote measurements that mostly appear in the HTML.\n\n221 passed and replaced the old trace. 34 were dropped (21 answers failed the runtime check, 13 traces failed the gates three times). **0 traces in v1.9 match the refusal pattern.** Answers are unchanged, word for word.\n\nThe other three.js rows, whose traces did not match the pattern keep their older traces and were not re-run through the runtime check for this release. Traces now come from more than one model.\n\nEvery trace contains a `验：` (check) step. Nothing here is a benchmark result.\n\nTrain on the gpt turn (reasoning \\+ answer); mask system and human.\n\n```python\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nds = load_dataset(\"sriq-ai/sriq-spatial-sft-v1.9\", split=\"train\")\n```\n\nCopy to bucket\n\nUse this dataset\n\n**Downloads last month**\n\n: 117\n\n[]()\n\nNumber of rows:\n\n1,532\n\n[]()\n\nTotal file size:\n\n82 MB\n\nSystem theme\n\nCompany\n\n[TOS](/terms-of-service) [Privacy](/privacy) [About](/huggingface) [Careers](https://apply.workable.com/huggingface/) [](/)\n\nWebsite\n\n[Models](/models) [Datasets](/datasets) [Spaces](/spaces) [Pricing](/pricing) [Docs](/docs)"

One row per conversation: the draft, the refinement, the request, and the reasoning trace.\n\nPipeline: [https://git.nixre.dev/sriq/svg-distill](https://git.nixre.dev/sriq/svg-distill) (Apache-2.0).\n\nThis is the agentic half of the corpus: the model sees the target image, calls tools to measure it, and edits the SVG until the render matches. It teaches the *procedure*, not the answer.\n\n> **Growing dataset.** This repo will keep growing: new rows are added and existing ones updated over time. Row counts below describe the current upload; pin a `revision` in `load_dataset` for a fixed snapshot.\n\n## [](#contents) Contents\n\n|  |  |\n| --- | --- |\n| **Rows** | 734 conversations |\n| **Turns** | system, user, assistant (with `tool_calls`), tool results |\n| **Images** | 9,968 files under `images/`, referenced from the messages as `images/<2 hex>/<hash>.png` |\n| **Messages** | 30,804 |\n| **Conversations** | 120 draft1, 118 prompt, 120 refine, 125 trace\\_img+text2svg, 127 trace\\_img2svg, 124 trace\\_text2svg |\n\n## [](#fields) Fields\n\n- `messages`: the conversation as it was sent, in OpenAI chat format. Tool calls, tool results and reasoning are kept; the inline images are replaced by files under `images/`.\n\n- `tools`: the tool schemas the model could call (`read_svg`, `edit_svg`, `sample_target`, `trace_region`, `zoom`).\n\n- `conv`: which conversation it is (`draft1`, `refine`, `prompt`, `trace_text2svg`, `trace_img2svg`, `trace_img+text2svg`).\n\n- `model`: the model that produced it. `source`: the target image. `url`: where that image came from. `run`: the run id.\n\n## [](#how-it-was-built) How it was built\n\n1. **Target.** A photo flattened into a simple flat-color version by an image-edit model.\n\n2. **Draft.** A vision model writes a complete SVG from the target.\n\n3. **Refine.** The same model improves it through tools: exact colors (`sample_target`), exact outlines (`trace_region`), close-ups (`zoom`). Every edit is scored against the target and reverted when it does not help. A text-only review then lists what is still wrong, and the model gets a budget of tool calls to fix it.\n\n4. **Request and trace.** A second model writes the request that would ask for the drawing; a third writes the reasoning trace from the finished SVG.\n\nNothing here is a benchmark result.\n\n```python\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nds = load_dataset(\"sriq-ai/sriq-svg-flow-v1.0\", split=\"train\")\n```\n\nCopy to bucket\n\nUse this dataset\n\n**Downloads last month**\n\n: 36\n\n[]()\n\nNumber of rows:\n\n734\n\n[]()\n\nTotal file size:\n\n1\\.2 GB\n\nSystem theme\n\nCompany\n\n[TOS](/terms-of-service) [Privacy](/privacy) [About](/huggingface) [Careers](https://apply.workable.com/huggingface/) [](/)\n\nWebsite\n\n[Models](/models) [Datasets](/datasets) [Spaces](/spaces) [Pricing](/pricing) [Docs](/docs)"

Each row asks for a drawing as one SVG file; the assistant turn is a compressed Simplified Chinese reasoning trace inside `<think>` tags, followed by the SVG. The reasoning is not the drawer's own: it is written by a second model from the finished SVG, and a gate checks it against that SVG.\n\nPipeline: [https://git.nixre.dev/sriq/svg-distill](https://git.nixre.dev/sriq/svg-distill) (Apache-2.0).\n\n> **Growing dataset.** This repo will keep growing: new rows are added and existing ones updated over time. Row counts below describe the current upload; pin a `revision` in `load_dataset` for a fixed snapshot.\n\n## [](#contents) Contents\n\n|  | Rows | Request | Answer | Median trace tokens | Median answer chars |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| text2svg | 118 | a synthetic request | one SVG file | 2,335.5 | 7,223.0 |\n| img2svg | 118 | the photo (as an `images` column) \\+ one instruction | one SVG file |  |  |\n| img+text2svg | 118 | the photo \\+ the synthetic request | one SVG file |  |  |\n| **Total** | **354** |  |  |  |  |\n\nDifficulty over all rows: 24 easy / 117 medium / 213 hard. 118 images, each exported as three records (the request alone, the photo alone, both). Token counts use `cl100k_base`. Median render-vs-target similarity of the drawings: 0\\.967.\n\n## [](#fields) Fields\n\n- `conversations`: system (`You are a helpful assistant`), human (the request), gpt (`<think>trace</think>` \\+ the SVG).\n\n- `images`: the photo of the image records, as bytes; empty for the text-only records.\n\n- `topic`: always `svg`. `language`: always `English` (the request language). `verification`: always `confirm` (every trace checks the drawing it describes; no planted mistakes in this set).\n\n- `difficulty`: the number of elements the drawing uses (easy \\< 30, medium \\< 55, hard \\>= 55).\n\n- `source`: the target image the drawing came from. `score`: the similarity of the render to that target.\n\nThe two extra columns (`source`, `score`) and `images` are new against [sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6); select the shared columns to concatenate with it.\n\n## [](#how-it-was-built) How it was built\n\n1. **Target.** A photo is flattened by an image-edit model into a simple flat-color version, and that is the drawing the model has to reproduce.\n\n2. **Drawing.** A vision model drafts an SVG, then improves it through tools (`read_svg`, `edit_svg`, `sample_target`, `trace_region`, `zoom`): exact colors and outlines instead of guesses. Every edit is scored against the target and reverted when it does not help, so the source is always the best one.\n\n3. **Request.** A second model sees the finished SVG and its render and writes the request that would ask for it. The image records show the original photo with one of 30 instructions, or with a short reference line plus that request.\n\n4. **Trace.** A separate call writes the reasoning from the finished SVG, in the SRIQ register: telegraphic Simplified Chinese, working notes, closing with a `验：` check. The gate rejects a trace without a `验：` that shows its arithmetic, a trace that is not mostly Chinese, one with pasted markup or refusal text, one that does not quote numbers of this SVG, and a `验：` that names no element of the SVG. A rejected trace is retried in place, not the whole row.\n\n353 of 354 rows carry a trace; the rest export the SVG without one.\n\nEvery trace contains a `验：` (check) step. Nothing here is a benchmark result.\n\nTrain on the gpt turn (reasoning \\+ answer); mask system and human.\n\n```python\nfrom datasets import load_dataset\nds = load_dataset(\"sriq-ai/sriq-svg-sft-v1.0\", split=\"train\")\n```\n\nCopy to bucket\n\nUse this dataset\n\n**Downloads last month**\n\n: 41\n\n[]()\n\nNumber of rows:\n\n354\n\n[]()\n\nTotal file size:\n\n249 MB\n\nSystem theme\n\nCompany\n\n[TOS](/terms-of-service) [Privacy](/privacy) [About](/huggingface) [Careers](https://apply.workable.com/huggingface/) [](/)\n\nWebsite\n\n[Models](/models) [Datasets](/datasets) [Spaces](/spaces) [Pricing](/pricing) [Docs](/docs)"

Each row asks for an object with switchable animations built only from procedural geometry. The assistant turn is a compressed Simplified Chinese reasoning trace inside `<think>` tags, followed by the answer. Same columns as [sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sriq-ai/sriq-sft-v1.6), so the two concatenate.\n\n## [](#contents) Contents\n\n| Source | Rows | Answer | easy / medium / hard | Median trace tokens | Median answer chars |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| three.js | 1,425 | one self-contained `.html` file (three.js from a CDN) | 357 / 628 / 440 | 5,287 | 40,747 |\n| OpenSCAD | 69 | one `.scad` file, animations driven by `$t` | 18 / 34 / 17 | 5,344 | 26,600 |\n| **Total** | **1,494** |  |  |  |  |\n\nToken counts use `cl100k_base`. The three.js rows come first, then the OpenSCAD rows.\n\n## [](#fields) Fields\n\n- `conversations`: system (`You are a helpful assistant`), human (the request), gpt (`<think>trace</think> answer`).\n\n- `topic`: always `spatial`. `language`: always `English` (the request language). `verification`: always `confirm`.\n\n- `difficulty`: requested structural complexity (simple → easy, moderate → medium, intricate → hard).\n\n## [](#how-it-was-built) How it was built\n\n1. **Seed.** An object and its animations are sampled from a pool of subjects crossed with era, region and scale.\n\n2. **Answer.** An undisclosed teacher model writes the answer. A second undisclosed model writes the trace from the finished code (the teacher's own reasoning is not available).\n\n3. **OpenSCAD rows** were rendered with the `openscad` CLI and rejected (or sent back to the teacher for repair) on any warning, error, or empty top-level object.\n\n4. **Dedup.** Near-duplicate objects in the three.js rows are dropped at export, keeping the earliest. The OpenSCAD rows are included in full.\n\n## [](#known-issues) Known issues\n\n- **250 of the 1,425 three.js traces (17.5%) match a refusal/meta pattern** (e.g. 「不能提供内部思维链。以下为基于成品的设计摘要。」, \"I can't give my internal chain of thought; here is a design summary\"). The pattern is broad (it also matches 摘要, \"summary\"), so some hits are false positives. None of the 69 OpenSCAD traces match. [Architecture](#architecture \"Architecture\")\n\n  - [CUDA loading and inference](#cuda-loading-and-inference \"CUDA loading and inference\")\n\n  - [Automatic lifetime and SQLite](#automatic-lifetime-and-sqlite \"Automatic lifetime and SQLite\")\n\n  - [Beam and multiple-return semantics](#beam-and-multiple-return-semantics \"Beam and multiple-return semantics\")\n\n  - [LoRA source and reproducible merge](#lora-source-and-reproducible-merge \"LoRA source and reproducible merge\")\n\n  - [Verified results](#verified-results \"Verified results\")\n\n  - [Limitations](#limitations \"Limitations\")\n\n# [](#spark-engram-v2-complete-spark-x25-4b-merged-checkpoint) Spark Engram V2: Complete Spark-X2.5-4B Merged Checkpoint\n\nThis checkpoint integrates Spark Engram V2's **automatic lifetime, surprise momentum, and bounded admission** with the Spark-X2.5-4B causal language model. It is the complete model produced by merging the trained LoRA adapter at step 100 and its saved Engram module into the original backbone.\n\nThe model contains **4,113,838,981 parameters**, including **1,759,621 Engram parameters**. Nine FP32 safetensors shards total **16,455,391,332 bytes (15.325 GiB)**; the tensor payload is 16,455,355,924 bytes. Config, tokenizer, generation config, weight index, and the Python modules required by Hugging Face `auto_map` are included. The original five backbone shards were preserved.\n\n## [](#architecture) Architecture\n\nThe backbone retains 36 Transformer layers, RMSNorm, GQA, RoPE, attention head gating, GELU-gated MLP, and its original full/sliding attention pattern. Engram sidecars at layers 1 and 5 combine static hashed embeddings, dynamic memory features, context gates, and causal depthwise convolution. Retrieved features affect an independent memory prediction and are not propagated through subsequent backbone attention or MLP layers. A separate baseline expert is retained for causal Bayesian calibration.\n\nInference-time fast state minimizes the local residual objective\n\nℓ(u;z)=12∥u−z∥22,∇uℓ=u−z, \\\\ell(u;z)=\\\\tfrac12\\\\\\|u-z\\\\\\|\\_2^2, \\\\qquad \\\\nabla\\_u\\\\ell=u-z,\n\nwith projected velocity momentum, forgetting, and an observation-indexed surprise EMA. The target is a normalized, detached slice of the current source-token embedding. New key/continuation pairs enter bounded probation. Admission requires repeated observations, sufficient surprise or velocity, and available row/cell capacity. Fast values, velocity, counts, and probation are inference state; static embeddings, projections, sidecars, and copy gate are model parameters.\n\nThis checkpoint allows 65,536 confirmed rows, 262,144 continuation cells, and 8,192 probation pairs per positional lane, with at most 16 lanes. The SQLite main file is capped at 256 MiB. That limit excludes rollback journals, weights, KV caches, logits, and working tensors. Existing confirmed associations remain updatable at capacity; new admission is rejected and counted. Storage failure raises an error and rolls back the transaction.\n\n## [](#cuda-loading-and-inference) CUDA loading and inference\n\nThe validated stack used Python 3\\.12.3, PyTorch 2\\.10.0+cu130 (CUDA 13\\.0), Transformers 5\\.8.0, PEFT 0\\.18.1, and Accelerate 1\\.11.0. Install a CUDA-enabled PyTorch build using the [official installation instructions](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/), then install the inference dependencies:\n\n```bash\npip install transformers==5.8.0 accelerate==1.11.0\n```\n\nPEFT is needed to reproduce the merge, but the complete merged model can be loaded directly. Set `<MODEL_DIR>` to this checkpoint directory:\n\n```python\nimport torch\nfrom transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer\n\nmodel_dir = \"<MODEL_DIR>\"\nassert torch.cuda.is_available()\ntokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_dir, trust_remote_code=True)\ntokenizer.padding_side = \"left\"\nmodel = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\n    model_dir, trust_remote_code=True,\n    dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map={\"\": \"cuda:0\"},\n).eval()\n\ninputs = tokenizer(\"The capital of France is\", return_tensors=\"pt\").to(\"cuda\")\nwith torch.inference_mode():\n    output = model(**inputs, use_cache=False)\n    answer = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=16, do_sample=False)\nprint(tokenizer.decode(answer[0, inputs.input_ids.shape[1]:]))\n```\n\n`AutoModelForCausalLM` resolves `Spark2_5ForCausalLM` through the bundled `auto_map`. Merging and saving used FP32 to preserve small weight updates; inference was verified with BF16 loading. The package also provides `TorchSparkForCausalLM` for native reference checkpoints; this 4B checkpoint uses the Hugging Face interface above.\n\n## [](#automatic-lifetime-and-sqlite) Automatic lifetime and SQLite\n\nThe saved configuration sets `memory_config.enable=true`, `mode=expandable`, `lifecycle=auto`, and namespace `Spark-X2.5-4B-v2-merged-checkpoint100`. With `storage_path=null`, the default location is\n\n```text\n$SPARK_ENGRAM_HOME/model-Spark-X2.5-4B-v2-merged-checkpoint100/memory.sqlite3\n```\n\nWithout `SPARK_ENGRAM_HOME`, the root is `$XDG_STATE_HOME/spark_engram`, falling back to `~/.local/state/spark_engram`. Set `SPARK_ENGRAM_HOME` before the model's first inference call, or provide `memory_config.storage_path` in the configuration before loading, to select a deployment location.\n\nOrdinary `forward` and `generate` calls restore, query, and commit memory automatically. A call without KV starts a fresh sequence boundary while retaining durable associations, preventing n-grams from crossing unrelated documents. Successful inference commits SQLite before returning. Training mode bypasses durable storage. A single observation can remain in probation and does not imply guaranteed recall.\n\n`save_pretrained` preserves model weights and memory configuration. SQLite is a separate file; copying the checkpoint alone does not transfer previously committed associations. Reloading the same checkpoint with the same bank location restores them.\n\nThe verified BPE example observes a 17-token source twice, reloads the checkpoint, and supplies only its 13-token prefix:\n\n```python\ntext = \"Archive key hazel-47: the recorded access phrase is cobalt lantern.\"\nids = tokenizer(text, add_special_tokens=False, return_tensors=\"pt\").input_ids.cuda()\nwith torch.inference_mode():\n    model(ids, use_cache=False)\n    model(ids, use_cache=False)\ndel model\ntorch.cuda.empty_cache()\nmodel = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\n    model_dir, trust_remote_code=True,\n    dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map={\"\": \"cuda:0\"},\n).eval()\nprefix = ids[:, :-4]\nwith torch.inference_mode():\n    answer = model.generate(prefix, max_new_tokens=4, do_sample=False)\nprint(tokenizer.decode(answer[0, prefix.shape[1]:]))  # \" cobalt lantern.\"\n```\n\n## [](#beam-and-multiple-return-semantics) Beam and multiple-return semantics\n\nEach original source prompt is observed once per generation call. Its committed table snapshot is shared by that source's beams or returns. Each decoded sequence has independent history, convolution buffers, calibration, pending predictions, and cursor state, synchronized with KV repeat/select/reorder operations. Different source lanes use separate banks. Model-generated continuations do not become new memory evidence by default.\n\nGreedy decoding, beam size 2, and sampling with two returns were verified. A lower-ranked beam hypothesis may differ from the best hypothesis. Batched generation uses left padding, with every source ending in a visible token; ordinary forward/SFT supports right padding. Generation requires KV and currently accepts the default/dynamic cache backend.\n\n## [](#lora-source-and-reproducible-merge) LoRA source and reproducible merge\n\nThe source adapter is the formal step-100 checkpoint. LLaMA-Factory 0\\.9.6.dev0 SFT used rank 16, alpha 32, targets `q_k_v_proj,out_proj`, and `modules_to_save=[\"engram\"]`. The two sources were `claude_opus_4_6_traceinversion_qwen35` (8,669 records) and `qwen38_27b_fp8_distillation_40k` (40,000 records). A prompt-group 95/5 split yielded 46,183 training and 2,486 holdout records.\n\nThe fixed run used 100 optimizer steps, BF16, cutoff 1024, packing=false, batch 1 with accumulation 4, learning rate 5e-5, cosine schedule, 5% warmup, non-reentrant gradient checkpointing, and seed/data seed 72001\\. It trained 10,606,981 parameters, including all Engram parameters. This artifact is a LoRA merge, with the remaining backbone tensors included in full. See the [training report](/win10/Spark-engram-4B-V2/blob/main/../../arxiv-sources/spark_engram_v2/docs/4B_TRAINING.md).\n\nThe merge loads the original backbone on CUDA, replaces all 17 initialized Engram tensors with the adapter's trained active module, and merges 72 LoRA target layers. PEFT unloading retains the active `modules_to_save` module. All 307 independent weight tensors are saved; embedding and LM head remain tied.\n\nA portable reproduction of the essential merge is:\n\n```bash\npip install peft==0.18.1 transformers==5.8.0 accelerate==1.11.0\n```\n\n```python\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport torch\nfrom peft import PeftModel\nfrom transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer\n\nbase_dir = \"<BASE_MODEL_DIR>\"  # V2-integrated Spark backbone with auto_map\nadapter_dir = \"<ADAPTER_DIR>\"  # trained formal checkpoint-100\noutput_dir = Path(\"<OUTPUT_DIR>\")\nassert torch.cuda.is_available()\nif output_dir.exists():\n    raise FileExistsError(\"Use a fresh output directory\")\nconfig = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(base_dir, trust_remote_code=True)\nconfig.memory_config = dict(\n    config.memory_config, enable=True, mode=\"expandable\", lifecycle=\"auto\",\n    storage_path=None, namespace=\"Spark-X2.5-4B-v2-merged-checkpoint100\",\n)\nbase = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\n    base_dir, config=config, trust_remote_code=True,\n    dtype=torch.float32, device_map={\"\": \"cuda:0\"},\n)\nadapted = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, adapter_dir, is_trainable=False)\nmerged = adapted.merge_and_unload(safe_merge=True)\nmerged.save_pretrained(output_dir, safe_serialization=True, max_shard_size=\"2GB\")\nAutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(adapter_dir, trust_remote_code=True).save_pretrained(output_dir)\n```\n\nThe source backbone's V2 Python dependencies must accompany the saved `auto_map`; this checkpoint includes that complete dependency bundle. The original base weights are read only, and the output uses a separate directory. `safe_merge` checks the LoRA merge for nonfinite values; reload validation additionally checks model loading and actual outputs.\n\n## [](#verified-results) Verified results\n\nMeasurements were recorded on NVIDIA Blackwell 96GB using CUDA PyTorch. All model parameters were on `cuda:0`. Both BF16 reloads had zero missing, unexpected, or mismatched keys and zero loading errors.\n\n| Check | Observed result |\n| --- | --- |\n| Complete model | 4,113,838,981 parameters; 307 independent tensors; 17 Engram tensors |\n| Merge integrity | All 72 LoRA deltas nonzero; sampled base weights changed; all trained Engram tensors loaded with zero difference |\n| Forward | Finite logits `[1,17,131072]`; range \\-41.204169 to \\-0.001044 |\n| General greedy execution | 16 output tokens; starts with ` Paris.\\nující `, followed by newlines; complete output is preserved in `observe.json` |\n| Exact-prefix recall | Two observations per record, then a different GPU process reload: 32/32, 100%, zero failures |\n| Four-token continuation | Greedy 1/1; beam 2 1/1; top-k-1 sampling with two returns 2/2, all ` cobalt lantern. ` |\n| Reader behavior | Independent transient state, shared same-source snapshot; 13 source-clock tokens added per call |\n\nThe 32 fixtures use actual BPE encoding of `Registry entry #NNNN => <word>`. Each final eight-token prefix address is unique, and the single-token answer is fixed in advance. The observing process exits before the query process loads the complete model and receives only prefixes. This establishes exact-prefix recall for those fixtures. General-language quality was not scored in the merge verification.\n\n| Phase | Peak allocated GiB | Peak reserved GiB |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| CUDA FP32 merge and save | 15\\.599 | 15\\.828 |\n| CUDA BF16 reload, forward, greedy, two observation passes | 7\\.767 | 7\\.781 |\n| Separate CUDA reload, 32 recalls, multi-sequence generation | 7\\.752 | 7\\.783 |\n\nThese are per-process PyTorch allocator peaks, excluding other processes' device occupancy. Anonymized evidence is available in [4B merged results](/win10/Spark-engram-4B-V2/tree/main/../../arxiv-sources/spark_engram_v2/results/4b-merged/). It includes merge, forward, recall, per-record predictions, and the original output-serialization error and recovery. That error occurred after successful observation and result persistence; observations were not repeated.\n\n## [](#limitations) Limitations\n\n- Retrieval uses exact-token prefix/n-gram addresses. Paraphrases and semantic QA are not guaranteed by these experiments.\n\n- SQLite banks use model/tokenizer namespace and positional source lane. They do not provide user authentication or cross-user isolation. Cooperating writers serialize transactions.\n\n- Speculative/assisted decoding, prompt lookup, self-speculative decoding, and KV crop lack transactional Engram cursor rollback and are rejected.\n\n- Bounded admission can reject useful new facts. The 256 MiB limit applies only to the SQLite main file.\n\n- `max_position_embeddings=1048576` remains the backbone configuration; million-token GPU inference, quality, and throughput were not measured.\n\n- Dynamic memory uses Python/SQLite processing. TP/DP sharding, fused memory kernels, and alternative cache backends were not validated.\n\n**Downloads last month**\n: 29\n\nSafetensors[](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors)\n\nModel size\n\n4B params\n\nTensor type\n\nF32\n\n·\n\nChat template\n\nFiles info\n\nInference Providers [NEW](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers)\n\nThis model isn't deployed by any Inference Provider. Boundary/date heads, static tables, dynamic projection, sidecars, backbone, and copy gate remain frozen. A new memory namespace isolates the updated evidence geometry; configured context and memory capacities are retained.\n\nEach update accumulates 20 microbatches: two trace QA (rotating over four sources), ten natural QA, four temporal QA, one recall, one order, and two SFT. QA is 80% of microbatches and natural QA is 50%. One eighth of QA microbatches supervise Unknown without observation. Every temporal relation has one slot per update. Recall/order replay weight is 2 and frozen round-two teacher SFT KL weight is 20\\.\n\nNatural QA uses five source groups per update and two different target fields per source. Source observation can be reused within the update; each question has independent reset reader state, a snapshot of evidence, and fresh KV. Target order is shuffled per document before its deterministic visit schedule, covering every source position during the declared run.\n\nData include 4,811 retained trace QA records, 7,718 natural questions across 1,200 training documents, and 3,200 temporal training questions. Natural training documents have 2 facts: 51, 4 facts: 178, 6 facts: 432, 8 facts: 539\\. Six/eight-fact documents account for 80\\.917% of training documents.\n\nNatural sources include same-noun/different-attribute and same-attribute/different-noun distractors, mixed fields, multiple sentence forms, reordered questions, and 4/5/6-digit identifiers with varying token lengths. Every fact has its own labeled question, with question form randomized independently of source position. Source-text parsing independently verifies answers; token offsets verify full copy spans and all candidate value starts. Hand-authored multi-fact and temporal reference cases validate labels without generator index logic. Wrong-label, wrong-span, wrong-candidate, and split-leak injections are rejected.\n\nThe fixed formal schedule contains 5,250 observed natural queries; 4,257 use six/eight facts. All first, middle, and final target positions are supervised. Training/development source groups, source text, and answer values are disjoint. New development question wording uses a held-out template family. All 256 evaluation questions and 448 fixed-suite values are excluded from QA and raw replay sources; the selected SFT replay inputs exclude the 32 NLL fixtures.\n\nNatural source-position CE weight is 1\\.5 (trace/temporal 0\\.5). Natural first-token contrastive CE over all observed candidate value starts has weight 1\\. Original-reader event CE weight is 0\\.2. First-token and EOS weights are each 3 in vocabulary and source-position CE; an additional final-token CE has weight 0\\.5. Full source-position supervision trains continuation within the selected value and a distinct EOS target after its last token. Candidate locations, answer spans, event IDs, and reference values enter only loss computation after model scores. Inference receives no labels, field rules, or answer lookup table.\n\nBF16 CUDA AMP; BF16 frozen backbone / FP32 Engram; AdamW, no weight decay, clipping 1, warmup 20, cosine schedule, seed 863033\\.
